pairs.evidence: examples/hirelane/design/check-contrast.mjs:178 When the contrast gate finds no token block to read it logs this line and exits 0, and check-law.mjs:219-220 does the same, so a moved or renamed tokens.css turns both law gates green instead of failing.

techniques.evidence: examples/hirelane/design/check-law.mjs:219 This breaks the zero-input-is-fatal clause in both checkers. Everything else is strong: colour literals are banned in every notation, the §9.4 exemption is loud and countable, a baseline ratchet exists, fixture tests watch the checks fail, and both run from the app's lint script.

examples/hirelane/design/check-law.mjs:100 The gate fails any numeric motion literal in a direction's TS. The board reads --bd-dur-* back from the cascade, so scripts hold no second copy. The header comment (lines 34-35) still calls motion.ts the numeric token block, which is now stale.

examples/hirelane/design/hl-scales.css:63 Easings are named by role (standard, entrance, exit, snap), and the stagger lives in the same vocabulary (line 60). The duration ladder has six numbered steps rather than categorical names.

pairs.subject: design-tokens
pairs.evidence: examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/level2/foot.css:111 Component sheets use steps of the graphite ramp directly (here graphite-4 as text on the inverted title block) instead of a role. The step's meaning changes with the ground it sits on, which is exactly the skipped-layer failure.

techniques.evidence: examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/level2/foot.css:111 About 100 var(--bk-graphite-N/vellum/sheet) uses across the level and chrome sheets. Only --bk-label-ink and the --dk-* bridge are roles.

examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/chrome/toast.css:24 A raw 3px where --bk-rule-3 exists (also the-sheet.css:86). The app's lint is eslint only and no raw-px or raw-value gate reads these sheets, unlike hirelane's check-law. The tests gate contrast per site and hover easing, not membership.
examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/base/tokens.css:160 A gated mirror: the --bk-beat-* tokens are checked against beats.ts, and --bk-label-w against useProjector by tidycrm-style.test.ts:311.

examples/tidycrm/components/blocks/style/base/tokens.css:173 The easing is named by curve shape ('in'), and the curve is actually decelerating, i.e. an entrance curve. The reduced-motion handling is conformant: a blanket near-zero 0.01ms block under .bk-root, plus delays zeroed (reduced-motion.css:7).
